note: mapping_basis=data_labels: item codes ARE the source column names P1120A-P1120F of REG11A (the .do keeps them verbatim, gen item = "`var'"; core model s3 pattern 1), and the data dictionary labels each variable (1120A 'a. realizar un trabajo pagado siempre, o a veces?' ... 1120F 'f. tomar decisiones sobre su cuerpo y/o métodos anticonceptivos'). Letters a-e agree between dictionary and printed questionnaire, 5/5 row texts identical. ROW F NOT IN THE PRINTED QUESTIONNAIRE: p.29 prints rows a-e only (checked on the rendered page image, not just the text layer) and goes straight to 1121F; the manual does not list rows. The dictionary's 1120F row and the data show f was administered (CAPI) to the same women: REG11A has P1120F answered by 971 women, the same 3276-2305 as a-e. P1120F's wording is therefore the dictionary label only; it is transcribed as the dictionary gives it (no closing '¿...siempre, o a veces?' tail and no question mark, unlike a-e), not harmonised. RESP: Bookmark 4 does NOT recode; it only sets 9 (NR) to missing. So live 1 = Siempre, 2 = A veces, 3 = Nunca, as printed and as in the dictionary (the (6=1)(1=2) reversal of the Sí/No siblings does not apply here). Route 9: raw REG11A counts (9 dropped) equal live in 18/18 item x resp cells unrecoded; a 1<->3 reversal would match only the 6 'A veces' cells. Live 1/2/3 = raw Siempre/A veces/Nunca: P1120A 157/142/671, P1120B 143/115/712, P1120C 144/121/704, P1120D 168/124/678, P1120E 147/129/693, P1120F 136/80/754. Dropped NR (9): 1,1,2,1,2,1. Live 5818 rows (the .do asserts 5818), 970 ids, per-item n 969-970. validate_items.R --table-sets PASS (6 items, resp {1,2,3}). TEXT (text_source=study_materials): item_text = the questionnaire's 1120 stem '¿Tiene usted que pedir permiso o contar con la aprobación de su esposo o pareja actual para…' joined to each row with a space, row letter dropped, line-break hyphen joined in e ('acti-vidad'); f's row from the dictionary. The row endings 'siempre, o a veces?' are printed on each row and kept verbatim. instructions blank: the only framing is the ENCUESTADORA box 'LEA CADA ALTERNATIVA PAUSADAMENTE Y MARQUE EL CÓDIGO “1” ó “2” ó “3” SEGÚN LA RESPUESTA DE LA INFORMANTE.', which is interviewer-facing. option_text = the printed column headers 'Siempre' / 'A veces' / 'Nunca' (dictionary agrees); no row for NR 9. Single section_id, no section_prompt. language=Spanish; translation_source=machine_translation: INE publishes the ENSIMUP in Spanish only; all English produced by IRW. STEP 3b: dictionary Description ('Whether the woman must ask her partner's permission to work, study, go out, see family or friends, or decide about her body') matches 1120 a-f; 6 live items = the 6 dictionary rows; 3-level resp = Siempre/A veces/Nunca.
